taxes._note: Frais d'achat d'un logement en Australie, par État/territoire (calculateur /australia). Chaque montant est relu le 14 oct. 2026 dans une page ou un document officiel (voir ~/Payotte/australie/rapports/phase-0/fiscalite.md). Contrôle : scripts/au/check-frais-achat.mjs. Un barème de ligne = base + taux % de la part du prix au-dessus de « de » (taux sur la totalité du prix : de = 0 et base = 0). « arrondi100 » : le texte officiel dit « per $100 or part of $100 ». Les montants non relus (page bloquée, formule non publiée) sont à null et expliqués dans « nonChiffre ».

source.note: Barème « 2026/2027 financial year » (page mise à jour le 6 oct. 2026) ; l'année du barème est fixée par la date du contrat. Tranche > 3 870 000 $ = « premium duty » résidentiel.

Contrats échangés à partir du 1er juillet 2023 : logement neuf ou existant exonéré jusqu'à 800 000 $, taux réduit au-dessus de 800 000 $ et sous 1 000 000 $. Le mode de calcul du taux réduit n'est pas publié sur les pages lues.

etranger.assiette: prix (dutiable value), en plus du droit de mutation

source.note: « Flat rate of 9% of the dutiable value » (surcharge purchaser duty), barème 2026/2027.

transfert.libelle: Transfer (pursuant to section 46 Real Property Act)

source.note: NSW Land Registry Services, Fees Update 2026/27 (émis juin 2026) ; colonnes Excl GST / Incl GST.
« $10,000 grant available for newly built or substantially renovated homes ». Plafonds de valeur non relus (document officiel illisible).
Contrats conclus à partir du 1er juillet 2021 ; page mise à jour le 29 sept. 2026. De 960 000 $ à 2 M$ : 5,5 % de la valeur totale.

Taux PPR pour contrats à partir du 6 mai 2008, valeur ≤ 550 000 $ ; installation sous 12 mois et résidence 12 mois (page https://www.sro.vic.gov.au/buying-property/land-transfer-stamp-duty/concessions-exemptions-and-waivers/principal-place-residence-duty-concession, mise à jour 24 juin 2026).

Page SRO (mise à jour 15 sept. 2026) : 0 $ jusqu'à 600 000 $, « reduced amount » de 600 001 à 750 000 $, sans formule. La formule ci-dessus est reconstituée depuis la Duties Act 2000 (Vic), s 57JA (version 141 du 24 juin 2026, PDF authentique https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/00-79aa141-authorised.pdf) : seuls les symboles A, B, 600 000 $ et 150 000 $ de la formule sont lisibles dans le texte extrait. À confirmer au calculateur SRO. Formule RETIRÉE le 14 oct. 2026 (non publiée par le SRO, aucune formule reconstituée) : le calculateur affiche le droit général comme borne haute.

etranger.assiette: prix, en plus du droit de mutation, avant toute concession

source.note: « The additional duty rate is 8% » ; la page ne donne pas de date d'entrée en vigueur (mise à jour 29 sept. 2026).
« A $10,000 grant … newly constructed or never-occupied properties valued up to $750,000 ».

Page mise à jour le 25 juin 2026 ; elle ne donne pas la date d'entrée en vigueur (elle renvoie à l'ancien barème pour les actes antérieurs au 21 sept. 2012). Exemple officiel : 850 000 $ (investissement) = 31 275 $.
Home concession rates. Exemple officiel : 950 000 $ = 28 600 $. Ne s'applique pas à la période du 1er août 2011 au 30 juin 2012.

First home concession (contrats à partir du 9 juin 2024) : déduction du droit au taux home concession. Logement neuf (« first home (new home) ») et terrain nu : concession totale, sans plafond de prix, pour les contrats à partir du 1er mai 2025 (conditions détaillées non lues). Exemple officiel : 795 000 $ = 19 890 $. Annonce du budget 2026-27 (QRO, 23 juin 2026) : à partir du 1er août 2026, ces concessions seront réservées aux citoyens, résidents permanents ou retraités étrangers désignés ; la page précise que les détails suivront « once the legislation passes » : INTENTION, non modélisée. MISE À JOUR (passe de cohérence, 14 oct. 2026) : restriction EN VIGUEUR — projet adopté le 26 juin, sanction royale le 29 juin 2026, applicable aux transactions signées à partir du 1er août 2026 (qro.qld.gov.au/event/changes-to-home-concessions ; page first-home mise à jour le 31 juil. 2026). Le calculateur écarte déjà les concessions pour un acheteur étranger.

source.note: « additional foreign acquirer duty (AFAD) of 8% on residential property, applied to the dutiable value ».

transfert.libelle: Lodging an instrument that changes the ownership of a lot (1 lot) + 46,56 $ par 10 000 $ ou fraction au-delà de 180 000 $

hypotheque.libelle: Poste (l) « any other instrument » : l'hypothèque n'est pas nommée dans le barème

source.note: Titles Queensland, Titles Registry Fees FY2026/27, Land Title Act 1994.

« grant of $15,000 or $30,000 » ; « The increased $30,000 grant will continue for eligible contracts signed from 1 July 2026 going forward » ; « new homes valued at less than $750,000 (including land) » (page du 30 juin 2026).
General rate, page mise à jour le 30 juil. 2026 ; pas de date d'entrée en vigueur sur la page.
Concessional rate : résidence principale ou actif commercial WA dont la valeur totale ne dépasse pas 200 000 $.

First home owner rate, transactions à partir du 7 mai 2026 : 0 $ jusqu'à 600 000 $ ; 16,15 $ par 100 $ (ou fraction) au-dessus de 600 000 $ jusqu'à 800 000 $ ; au-delà, barème général. Les seuils valent pour la valeur totale du bien.

etranger.assiette: part du prix acquise par la personne étrangère, en plus du droit de mutation

source.note: Seul le taux de 7 % est lu, dans l'exemple officiel de cette page (200 000 $ × 7 % = 14 000 $). Date d'entrée en vigueur et page dédiée INTROUVABLES.
Landgate, Search and Lodgement Fees Payable as at 1 July 2026 ; frais non soumis à la GST.
« up to $10,000 » ; plafond de valeur 800 000 $ au sud du 26e parallèle (1 000 000 $ au nord) pour les transactions à partir du 7 mai 2026 (page du 29 juil. 2026).

Page SA Government : « you'll pay zero stamp duty when you build or buy a new home » (logement neuf, appartement sur plan, terrain à bâtir), seuils de valeur supprimés. Le logement existant n'est pas couvert (texte RevenueSA illisible : 403).
« You can receive up to $15,000 » pour un logement neuf.

sa.nonChiffre: Barème des droits : revenuesa.sa.gov.au, legislation.sa.gov.au et dhud.sa.gov.au répondent 403 (non contourné). Aucune autre page officielle lisible : barème, surtaxe étrangère et frais d'enregistrement non chiffrés.

source.note: « Rates for transfers on or after 21 October 2013 » ; page publiée le 14/06/2022. Le Taxation and Related Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2026 (en vigueur le 9 oct. 2026, SRO) modifie le droit de mutation : son contenu n'a pas été lu.

Exonération (logement existant ≤ 750 000 $) pour règlements du 18 févr. 2024 au 30 juin 2026 : « not available for transactions settling after 30 June 2026 ». Aucune prolongation sur la page (publiée le 16/07/2026).

etranger.assiette: part de la valeur imposable du bien résidentiel acquise par la personne étrangère, en plus du droit

source.note: 8 % pour les accords à partir du 1er avril 2020 (3 % avant) ; page publiée le 29/06/2022.
Land Titles Office, Brief Schedule of Fees.
Accueil SRO (publié 12 oct. 2026) : « The $20,000 grant took effect from 1 July 2026 » ; conditions (logement neuf) non relues sur page dédiée.

Explanatory statement du Taxation Administration (Amounts Payable—Duty) Determination 2026 (DI2026-155) : taux marginaux par 100 $ ou fraction, colonnes occupant (4) / autre (5) ; les bases cumulées sont recalculées à partir de ces taux (contrôle : 11 400 $ à 500 000 $ pour le non-occupant, 8 408 $ pour l'occupant, tels que publiés). Au-delà de 1 455 000 $ : taux plat sur toute la valeur. Exemple publié : 580 000 $ = 14 856 $ (autre) ; l'occupant y est imprimé 11 128 $, incohérent avec sa propre base de 8 408 $ (8 408 + 3 456 = 11 864 $).

Eligible owner occupier transaction : personne physique, un acquéreur au moins occupe le bien comme résidence principale en continu pendant au moins un an, à partir de 12 mois après la remise des clés.

Taxation Administration (Amounts Payable—Home Buyer Concession Scheme) Determination 2026 (DI2026-157), s 7 : « nil rate of duty » pour une transaction éligible ; s 6 : date de transaction ≥ 1er juillet 2026, aucun intérêt foncier détenu par l'acheteur ni son partenaire dans les 5 dernières années, un acheteur occupe le bien (résidence, annexe 2) ; aucun plafond de prix ni de revenu dans ce texte (PDF https://legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/di/2026-157/current/PDF/2026-157.PDF).

hypotheque.libelle: Land Titles Act 1925 s 92, application to register a mortgage or encumbrance

act.nonChiffre: Surtaxe acheteur étranger : aucune mention dans l'explanatory statement lu ; pages revenue.act.gov.au répondent 403 (non contourné) : INTROUVABLE, non chiffrée.

source.note: Stamp Duty Act 1978, Schedule 1 clause 1(2), texte « as in force at 1 July 2025 » (reprint REPS013). D = 0,06571441 × V² + 15 × V, V = valeur / 1000, jusqu'à 525 000 $ ; 4,95 % de 525 001 $ à moins de 3 M$ ; 5,75 % de 3 M$ à moins de 5 M$ ; 5,95 % au-delà. Les pages treasury.nt.gov.au et nt.gov.au répondent 403 : modifications postérieures au 1er juillet 2025 non vérifiées.

Stamp Duty Act 1978 s 88 et 89AAB, « Territory home owner discount » : déduction égale au moindre du droit ou de 18 601 $, si la valeur imposable ne dépasse pas le seuil (650 000 $ sauf montant fixé par règlement), pour les actes à partir du 8 févr. 2019 ; conditions (citoyen ou résident permanent, 18 ans, pas d'intérêt résidentiel au NT dans les 24 mois, résidence). Texte « as in force at 1 July 2025 », règlement éventuel non lu.

nt.nonChiffre: Aucune surtaxe acheteur étranger dans le Stamp Duty Act 1978 lu (le mot « foreign » n'y désigne que les assureurs). House and Land Package Exemption (contrats du 1er juil. 2022 au 30 juin 2027), HomeGrown Territory Grant et frais du Land Titles Office : pages officielles 403, INTROUVABLES, non chiffrés.

apra.limiteDTI: au plus 20 % des nouveaux prêts avec un DTI de 6 ou plus, depuis février 2026

depot5.nom: Australian Government 5% Deposit Scheme (ex-Home Guarantee Scheme)

source.note: Dépôt minimum 5 % (2 % parents seuls), sans plafond de revenu, sans liste d'attente ; demande auprès d'un prêteur participant. Annonce : https://www.pm.gov.au/media/uncapped-5-cent-deposits-available-first-home-buyers-today (1er oct. 2025). Plafonds de prix par région : INTROUVABLES sur pages lues (housingaustralia.gov.au répond 403).

Schedule of Fees v8, tables 2 et 3 (« Less than $75,000 » puis tranche d'un million) ; interdiction d'achat de logements existants par des étrangers : Australia's foreign investment policy, mai 2026 (https://foreigninvestment.gov.au/sites/foreigninvestment.gov.au/files/2026-05/australias-foreign-investment-policy-may-2026.pdf) : « commenced on 1 April 2025 and will be in place until 30 June 2029 ».

taxes.nonChiffre: Honoraires de conveyancer / solicitor, courtier et inspection : aucun barème officiel, non chiffrés. Frais d'enregistrement non relus : VIC (Land Services Victoria, 403), SA (Land Services SA, table au millésime ambigu), NT.

nsw.length: 5 business days (10 for off the plan)
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, the cooling-off period is 5 business days from exchange of contracts (10 for off the plan), and withdrawing costs 0.25% of the price. There is none at auction.

sources.title: Contracts and deposits when buying property in NSW (nsw.gov.au)
Buying property at an auction (nsw.gov.au)

vic.cost_to_withdraw: refund less the greater of $100 or 0.2% of the price
vic.answer: In Victoria, the cooling-off period is 3 clear business days from signing a private sale contract. The buyer is refunded less the greater of $100 or 0.2% of the price, and there is none at auction.

sources.title: Buying property by private sale (Consumer Affairs Victoria)

qld.answer: In Queensland, the cooling-off period is 5 business days from receiving the contract signed by both parties, ending at 5pm. The seller may keep up to 0.25% of the price, and there is none at auction.

sources.title: Cooling-off period for residential property contracts (qld.gov.au)
Cooling-off period (qld.gov.au, buyer guide)

wa.answer: Western Australia has no mandatory cooling-off period for real estate contracts. The parties can agree to insert one in the contract, so a buyer who wants one must negotiate it before signing.
wa.note: Cost applies only if a clause is agreed; auctions not addressed in the guide.

sources.title: Sale by offer and acceptance (Consumer Protection WA)

sa.answer: In South Australia, the cooling-off period is 2 business days from service of the Form 1, or from signing if the Form 1 came first. There is none at auction.
sa.note: Cost to withdraw not described in the guide; source page last revised December 2013.

sources.title: Cooling-off period (SA Law Handbook)

tas.answer: Tasmania's Property Agents and Land Transactions Act 2016 (version of 1 July 2025) contains no cooling-off provision, so any cooling-off would come from the contract itself.
tas.note: No statutory period found; check the contract.

sources.title: Property Agents and Land Transactions Act 2016 (Tasmania), authorised version 1 July 2025

act.answer: In the ACT, the cooling-off period ends at 5pm on the 5th working day after it begins, and the buyer forfeits 0.25% of the price. There is none at auction or tender.

sources.title: Civil Law (Sale of Residential Property) Act 2003 (ACT), republication 1 November 2025

nt.answer: For the Northern Territory, the guide could not read the NT Government pages, so the length and cost of any cooling-off period are not stated. Ask the NT Government or an NT conveyancer.
nt.note: Guide notes a rule exists for property not sold by auction; length and start not read.

sources.title: Contracts and deposits when buying property in NSW (nsw.gov.au)

nsw.conditions: contracts exchanged from 1 July 2023; move in within 12 months of settlement and live there for 12 continuous months; vacant land is nil up to $350,000 and reduced up to $450,000
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, first home buyers pay no duty on a new or existing home up to $800,000, with a concessional rate from there up to $1,000,000. Vacant land is nil up to $350,000 and reduced below $450,000.

sources.title: First Home Buyers Assistance Scheme (Revenue NSW)

vic.conditions: individuals aged 18 or over; at least one an Australian citizen, New Zealand citizen or permanent resident; no prior grant or duty benefit, no home owned before 1 July 2000 or lived in for 6 months or more since (check the SRO wording); live there 12 continuous months starting within 12 months of settlement; all buyers on the Victorian electoral roll
vic.answer: In Victoria, first home buyers pay no duty on a home up to $600,000 and a reduced amount from $600,001 to $750,000. The buyer must live in the home for 12 continuous months, starting within 12 months of settlement.

sources.title: First home buyer duty exemption or concession (State Revenue Office Victoria)

qld.conditions: individual aged 18 or over; never held an interest in a residence anywhere in the world; move in within 1 year; from 1 August 2026 citizens, permanent residents or specified foreign retirees only; no value cap for a new first home or first home vacant land (from 1 May 2025)
qld.answer: In Queensland, a first home buyer pays no duty on a home up to $700,000 (contracts from 9 June 2024), and the concession fades to nil at $800,000. A new first home or first home vacant land has no value cap from 1 May 2025.

sources.title: First home concession (Queensland Revenue Office)
Transfer duty home concession rates (Queensland Revenue Office)

wa.conditions: qualify for the first home owner grant criteria (or the listed exceptions); tell the Commissioner within 30 days if a criterion will not be met; vacant land is nil up to $450,000 and reduced up to $550,000
wa.answer: In Western Australia, for agreements from 7 May 2026, a first home owner pays no duty on a home up to $600,000 and $16.15 per $100 above $600,000 up to $800,000. Vacant land is nil up to $450,000.

sources.title: Duties Fact Sheet: First Home Owner Rate (Government of Western Australia)

sa.conditions: eligible first home buyers only; new home, off-the-plan apartment, house and land package or vacant land to build on; not an established home; dates and conditions published by RevenueSA
sa.answer: In South Australia, eligible first home buyers pay zero stamp duty on a new home, off-the-plan apartment, house and land package or vacant land to build on, with no value threshold. The relief does not cover an established home.
sa.note: Relief covers new homes only; no partial band.

sources.title: Home buyer support (HomeSeeker SA, Government of South Australia)
FAQs (HomeSeeker SA, Government of South Australia)

tas.conditions: the 100% established-home exemption (homes up to $750,000) applied only to settlements from 18 February 2024 to 30 June 2026
tas.answer: In Tasmania, the first home buyer duty exemption for established homes is not available for settlements after 30 June 2026, and the State Revenue Office names no replacement. It was a 100% exemption for homes up to $750,000.
tas.note: Ended 30 June 2026, so no current threshold.

sources.title: First home buyers of established homes duty relief (State Revenue Office Tasmania)
Concessions and exemptions (State Revenue Office Tasmania)

act.conditions: individuals aged 18 or over; no interest in land held by any buyer or domestic partner in the previous 5 years; occupy as principal residence for 1 continuous year; transaction date on or after 1 July 2026
act.answer: In the ACT, an eligible home buyer pays nil duty on a home or vacant land for transactions on or after 1 July 2026, with no income or value limit in the determination. Buyers who do not meet the test pay the owner-occupier scale.
act.note: No partial band; the determination sets no value limit.

sources.title: Taxation Administration (Amounts Payable—Home Buyer Concession Scheme) Determination 2026, DI2026-157 (ACT Legislation Register)

nt.conditions: citizen or permanent resident; no residential property in the Territory in the previous 24 months; value at most the threshold ($650,000 unless a regulation prescribes another); 6 months of residence
nt.answer: In the Northern Territory, the Territory home owner discount cuts duty by the lesser of the duty assessed and $18,601 for eligible buyers whose home is worth at most $650,000. It is not limited to first home buyers.
nt.note: Discount rather than an exemption; threshold is the default unless a regulation sets another.

sources.title: Stamp Duty Act 1978, as in force at 1 July 2025 (NT Legislation)

nsw.price_cap: $600,000 for a new or renovated home; $750,000 for land plus building contract combined
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, the First Home Owner Grant is $10,000 for a new or substantially renovated home worth up to $600,000, or up to $750,000 for a land plus building contract. The buyer must live there for 12 continuous months.

sources.title: First Home Owner (New Homes) Grant (Revenue NSW)

vic.answer: In Victoria, the First Home Owner Grant is $10,000 for a new home worth up to $750,000 that has never been sold, occupied, leased or used for short-term accommodation. The buyer must live there 12 months.

sources.title: Understanding the First Home Owner Grant (State Revenue Office Victoria)

qld.answer: In Queensland, the First Home Owner Grant is $30,000 for a new home valued at less than $750,000, including land and contract variations, for contracts from 20 November 2023. The 2026 State Budget page says the grant is continued for contracts from 1 July 2026.
qld.note: Continuation from 1 July 2026 is announced; legislated position to be checked with the QRO.

sources.title: First home owner grant eligibility criteria (Queensland Revenue Office)
State Budget 2026 (Queensland Revenue Office)

wa.price_cap: $800,000 south of the 26th parallel; $1,000,000 north (transactions from 7 May 2026)
wa.answer: In Western Australia, the First Home Owner Grant is up to $10,000 for a new or substantially renovated home. For transactions from 7 May 2026 the value cap is $800,000 south of the 26th parallel and $1,000,000 north of it.

sources.title: About the first home owner grant (Government of Western Australia)

sa.answer: In South Australia, the First Home Owner Grant is up to $15,000 for buying or building a new home that will be the principal place of residence.
sa.note: Price cap not stated in the guide; check RevenueSA.

sources.title: Home buyer support (HomeSeeker SA, Government of South Australia)
FAQs (HomeSeeker SA, Government of South Australia)

tas.answer: In Tasmania, the First Home Owner Grant is $20,000 for an eligible transaction commencing on or after 1 July 2026 and before 1 July 2027, completed within 24 months. It is for a newly built home or building a new residence.
tas.note: Price cap not stated in the guide.

sources.title: First Home Owner Grant Amendment Act 2026, No. 9 of 2026 (Tasmanian legislation)
First Home Owner (State Revenue Office Tasmania)

act.answer: In the ACT, the First Home Owner Grant amount has been a nil amount since 1 July 2019. ACT home buyers use the duty concession scheme instead.
act.note: No grant, so no property rule or price cap.

sources.title: First Home Owner Grant (Amount) Determination 2019 (No 1), DI2019-138 (ACT Legislation Register)

nt.answer: In the Northern Territory, the First Home Owner Grant is $50,000 for transactions commencing from 1 October 2025 to before 1 October 2027, and $10,000 from 1 October 2027. Only a new home qualifies for purchase contracts since 1 October 2025.
nt.note: No price threshold applies to current transactions.

sources.title: First Home Owner Grant Act 2000, as in force at 1 July 2026 (NT Legislation)

nsw.name: Surcharge purchaser duty
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, a foreign person buying residential land pays surcharge purchaser duty of 9% of the dutiable value on top of transfer duty. On a $1,000,000 purchase that is $90,000.

sources.title: What is surcharge purchaser duty (Revenue NSW)

vic.name: Foreign purchaser additional duty
vic.answer: In Victoria, foreign purchasers pay 8% additional duty on agreements entered into on or after 1 July 2019, calculated on the foreign purchaser's share of the dutiable value.

sources.title: Foreign purchaser additional duty, current rates (State Revenue Office Victoria)
Understanding foreign purchaser additional duty (State Revenue Office Victoria)

qld.name: Additional foreign acquirer duty (AFAD)
qld.answer: In Queensland, foreign acquirers of residential land pay 8% additional foreign acquirer duty. From 1 August 2026 temporary residents also lose home concessions.

sources.title: Transfer duty rates (Queensland Revenue Office)
First home concession (Queensland Revenue Office)

wa.name: Foreign transfer duty
wa.answer: In Western Australia, foreign persons buying residential property pay 7% foreign transfer duty, even where the first home owner rate applies. On a $400,000 joint purchase with a 50% foreign share it is $14,000.

sources.title: Foreign transfer duty (Government of Western Australia)
2026-27 Housing Taxation Package (Government of Western Australia)

sa.answer: Payotte could not read the RevenueSA pages, so whether South Australia charges a foreign purchaser surcharge, and at what rate, is not stated here. Ask RevenueSA before signing.

sources.title: Foreign Investment (foreigninvestment.gov.au)

tas.name: Foreign investor duty surcharge
tas.answer: In Tasmania, the foreign investor duty surcharge is 8% on residential property from 1 April 2020 and 1.5% on primary production property, on the share acquired by the foreign person.

sources.title: Rates of surcharge, foreign investor duty surcharge (State Revenue Office Tasmania)

act.answer: In the ACT, no residential foreign-purchaser surcharge was found in the Duties Act 1999 or the 2026 determinations. Federal approval is still required for foreign persons.
act.note: Based on a text search of the Act.

sources.title: Duties Act 1999 (ACT Legislation Register)

nt.answer: In the Northern Territory, no residential foreign-purchaser surcharge was found in the Stamp Duty Act 1978 (version of 1 July 2025). Federal approval is still required for foreign persons.
nt.note: Based on a text search of the Act.

sources.title: Stamp Duty Act 1978, as in force at 1 July 2025 (NT Legislation)

nsw.absentee_surcharge: 5% (surcharge land tax for foreign persons, from 2025)
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, land tax starts above a land value of $1,075,000 (frozen since 2025) and a foreign person pays a 5% surcharge. A principal place of residence is exempt if the occupants own at least 25%.

sources.title: Land tax thresholds and rates (Revenue NSW)
Land tax exemption for principal place of residence (Revenue NSW)
What is surcharge land tax? (Revenue NSW)

vic.answer: In Victoria, land tax starts at $50,000 of site value and absentee owners pay a 4% surcharge. A principal place of residence is not charged land tax.

sources.title: Land tax, current rates (State Revenue Office Victoria)
Principal place of residence exemption (State Revenue Office Victoria)

qld.answer: In Queensland, land tax for individuals starts at $600,000, and absentee individuals pay a 3% surcharge on value above $350,000. The home exemption covers a principal place of residence on one parcel.
qld.note: Scale year not named on the QRO page (last updated 23 July 2024).

sources.title: Land tax, calculate for individuals (Queensland Revenue Office)
Land tax, calculate for absentees (Queensland Revenue Office)
Land tax, home exemption test (Queensland Revenue Office)

wa.answer: In Western Australia, land tax starts at $300,000 of unimproved value, plus a Metropolitan Region Improvement Tax on Perth-area land above $300,000. A private residence used as primary residence is exempt.
wa.note: The page read does not mention a foreign land tax surcharge.

sources.title: Land tax (Government of Western Australia)
Land tax fact sheet, private residences (Government of Western Australia)
Overview of State Taxes and Royalties 2025-26 (WA Department of Treasury and Finance, November 2025)

sa.answer: In South Australia, land tax starts at $833,001 in 2025-26, indexed each year, at 0.5% up to 2.4% above $3.116m. For 2026-27 amounts and the home exemption, check Revenue SA.
sa.note: Home exemption and surcharge not covered by the guide.

sources.title: Overview of State Taxes and Royalties 2025-26 (WA Department of Treasury and Finance, November 2025)

tas.absentee_surcharge: 2% (foreign investor surcharge, land acquired from 1 July 2022)
tas.answer: In Tasmania, land tax starts at $125,000, and a 2% surcharge applies to foreign persons who acquired residential land from 1 July 2022. Principal residence land is not subject to land tax.

sources.title: Rates of land tax (State Revenue Office Tasmania)
Land tax (State Revenue Office Tasmania)
Foreign investor land tax surcharge factsheet (State Revenue Office Tasmania)

act.answer: In the ACT, land tax is a fixed fee ($1,693 in 2025-26) plus marginal rates, with a 0.75% surcharge on residential land owned by foreign non-residents. Check the ACT Revenue Office for 2026-27 amounts.
act.note: Home exemption not covered by the guide.

sources.title: Overview of State Taxes and Royalties 2025-26 (WA Department of Treasury and Finance, November 2025)

nt.answer: The Northern Territory does not levy land tax, according to the 2025-26 Western Australian Treasury overview. Council rates are separate.
nt.note: No land tax, so no exemption or surcharge.

sources.title: Overview of State Taxes and Royalties 2025-26 (WA Department of Treasury and Finance, November 2025)

nsw.answer: In New South Wales, transfer duty is collected by Revenue NSW: at general rates it comes to $21,187 on a $600,000 home, $30,187 on $800,000 and $39,187 on $1,000,000, plus a 9% surcharge for foreign buyers.

sources.title: Revenue NSW: current rates
Revenue NSW: foreign purchasers

vic.answer: In Victoria, land transfer duty is collected by State Revenue Office Victoria: at general rates it comes to $31,070 on a $600,000 home, $43,070 on $800,000 and $55,000 on $1,000,000, plus a 8% surcharge for foreign buyers.

sources.title: State Revenue Office Victoria: current rates
State Revenue Office Victoria: foreign purchasers

qld.answer: In Queensland, transfer duty is collected by Queensland Revenue Office: at general rates it comes to $20,025 on a $600,000 home, $29,025 on $800,000 and $38,025 on $1,000,000, plus a 8% surcharge for foreign buyers.

sources.title: Queensland Revenue Office: current rates
Queensland Revenue Office: foreign purchasers

wa.answer: In Western Australia, transfer duty is collected by RevenueWA (Department of Finance): at general rates it comes to $22,515 on a $600,000 home, $32,315.50 on $800,000 and $42,615.50 on $1,000,000, plus a 7% surcharge for foreign buyers.

sources.title: RevenueWA (Department of Finance): current rates
RevenueWA (Department of Finance): foreign purchasers

sa.answer: In South Australia, the duty on a home purchase is stamp duty on conveyances, collected by RevenueSA; Payotte does not compute it because the official rate pages could not be read.

tas.answer: In Tasmania, property transfer duty is collected by State Revenue Office Tasmania: at general rates it comes to $22,497.50 on a $600,000 home, $31,185 on $800,000 and $40,185 on $1,000,000, plus a 8% surcharge for foreign buyers.

sources.title: State Revenue Office Tasmania: current rates
State Revenue Office Tasmania: foreign purchasers

act.answer: In Australian Capital Territory, conveyance duty is collected by ACT Revenue Office: at general rates it comes to $15,720 on a $600,000 home, $25,150 on $800,000 and $36,950 on $1,000,000.
act.note: Non owner-occupier rates; eligible owner-occupiers pay less.

sources.title: ACT Revenue Office: current rates

nt.answer: In Northern Territory, stamp duty on conveyances is collected by Territory Revenue Office: at general rates it comes to $29,700 on a $600,000 home, $39,600 on $800,000 and $49,500 on $1,000,000.
nt.note: Stamp Duty Act as in force at 1 July 2025; later changes not checked.

sources.title: Territory Revenue Office: current rates

nsw.answer: In New South Wales, the rental bond is capped at 4 weeks' rent, with no separate pet bond, and is held by NSW Fair Trading.
nsw.note: Lodgement deadline not stated on the pages the guide read.

sources.title: Costs at the start of a residential tenancy (NSW Government)
Lodge a residential rental bond, landlords and agents (Service NSW)

vic.cap: one month's rent (more if rent is over $900 a week, or VCAT sets it)
vic.answer: In Victoria, the bond is generally capped at one month's rent, or more if rent exceeds $900 a week. The rental provider must lodge it with the RTBA within 14 days, not counting public holidays.

sources.title: Bond amounts and payments (Consumer Affairs Victoria)
Lodging the bond with the RTBA (Consumer Affairs Victoria)

qld.answer: In Queensland, the bond is capped at 4 weeks' rent for agreements signed on or after 30 September 2024, and must be lodged with the RTA within 10 days.

sources.title: Rental bond (Residential Tenancies Authority, Queensland)
Rental bonds fact sheet (Residential Tenancies Authority, Queensland)

wa.cap: 4 weeks' rent (rent up to $1,200 a week)
wa.answer: In Western Australia, the bond is capped at 4 weeks' rent where rent is $1,200 a week or less, and must be lodged with Bonds Administration within 14 days. A pet bond of up to $350 is allowed.

sources.title: Rental bonds (Consumer Protection WA)
Lodging a bond (Consumer Protection WA)

sa.cap: 4 weeks' rent if rent is $800 a week or less; 6 weeks above
sa.authority: Commissioner, via Consumer and Business Services
sa.answer: In South Australia, the bond cap is 4 weeks' rent where rent is $800 a week or less and 6 weeks above that. The landlord must lodge within 2 weeks and a registered agent within 4 weeks.

sources.title: Residential Tenancies, chapter 23 (South Australia Law Handbook)

tas.answer: In Tasmania, a landlord must not require a deposit above 4 weeks' rent. It is paid to the Rental Deposit Authority, or to a property agent who must pass it on within 10 working days.

sources.title: Residential Tenancy Act 1997 (Tasmanian legislation)

act.lodge_within: later of 2 weeks and the tenancy start (lessor); later of 4 weeks and the tenancy start (agent)
act.answer: In the ACT, a bond cannot exceed 4 weeks' rent and is lodged with the Office of Rental Bonds. The lessor's deadline is the later of 2 weeks and the start of the tenancy, or 4 weeks for an agent.

sources.title: Residential Tenancies Act 1997, republication 84 effective 26 November 2025 (ACT legislation)

nt.authority: Landlord, in trust (Act as at 1 August 2025)
nt.answer: In the Northern Territory, the bond cannot exceed 4 weeks' rent, worked out on the lowest weekly rent. On the Act as at 1 August 2025 the landlord holds it in a trust account.
nt.note: No lodgement deadline: the landlord holds the bond.

sources.title: Residential Tenancies Act 1999, as in force at 1 August 2025 (NT legislation)

nsw.contents: property certificate (title search), registered plan and recorded dealings, drainage diagram, section 10.7 zoning certificate, statement of cooling-off rights, pool certificate where applicable
nsw.answer: In New South Wales, the seller must attach disclosure documents to the contract before exchange, such as a title search, drainage diagram and zoning certificate. If they are missing the buyer may withdraw within 14 days of exchange, unless settlement has occurred.

sources.title: Steps to selling a property (nsw.gov.au)
Selling a property (nsw.gov.au)

vic.contents: title, mortgages, covenants, easements, zoning, outgoings, bushfire-prone declaration, owners corporation certificate for lots; not the condition of buildings
vic.answer: In Victoria, the seller must give the buyer a section 32 vendor's statement before the buyer signs. A contract is not binding on the buyer if it is missing, incomplete or inaccurate.
vic.note: A reform on timing is passed but not yet in force (latest start 1 June 2027).

sources.title: Conveyancing and contracts for sellers (Consumer Affairs Victoria)
Contracts and disclosure statements (Consumer Affairs Victoria)

qld.contents: seller and property details, title and encumbrances, land use and planning, buildings and structures; prescribed certificates (title search, notices, pool safety, body corporate)
qld.answer: In Queensland, since 1 August 2025 the seller must give a Form 2 disclosure statement and prescribed certificates before the buyer signs. The buyer may terminate up to settlement if documents are not given.

sources.title: Seller disclosure scheme (Queensland Government)
Contract of sale for buying a home (Queensland Government)

wa.document: None mandatory (strata lots: pre-contractual disclosure statement)
wa.answer: In Western Australia there is no mandatory seller disclosure statement for ordinary homes, though the agent must disclose relevant facts. For a strata lot, the seller must give a pre-contractual disclosure statement before the buyer signs.
wa.note: Contents not listed in the guide.

sources.title: Real estate contracts: sale by offer and acceptance (Consumer Protection WA)
Resources for strata sellers (Landgate)

sa.answer: In South Australia, the vendor must serve a Form 1 statement at least 10 days before settlement, with a fine of up to $10,000 for failing to serve a correct one. A defective Form 1 does not start cooling-off and the buyer may rescind until settlement.
sa.note: Contents of the Form 1 not described in the guide; source predates the 2025 regulations.

sources.title: Form 1 (SA Law Handbook)

tas.answer: For Tasmania, the Conveyancing and Law of Property Act 1884 imposes no pre-contract disclosure statement in the parts the guide read, and no other vendor disclosure rule could be confirmed.
tas.note: Not confirmed from an official source; ask CBOS or a conveyancer.

sources.title: Conveyancing and Law of Property Act 1884 (Tasmanian Legislation)

act.document: Required documents under the Civil Law (Sale of Residential Property) Act 2003
act.contents: proposed contract, Crown lease, certified land titles extract, deposited plan, encumbrances, building conveyancing inquiry documents, energy efficiency rating statement, building and compliance inspection report, pest inspection report if occupied
act.answer: In the ACT, the seller must give the buyer a set of required documents before the contract, including an energy efficiency rating statement. A seller who omits the statement is liable to pay the buyer 0.5% of the price.

sources.title: Civil Law (Sale of Residential Property) Act 2003, republication 32, effective 1 November 2025 (ACT legislation)

nt.document: Particulars of title under the Law of Property Act 2000
nt.answer: In the Northern Territory, the Law of Property Act 2000 entitles a purchaser of registered land to particulars of title at the vendor's cost, but the guide did not find a statutory disclosure statement.
nt.note: No NT disclosure statement read; ask the NT Government or a conveyancer.

sources.title: Law of Property Act 2000, as in force at 2 January 2024 (NT legislation)

guides.title: Building and pest inspection before you buy
guides.description: What a pre-purchase building and pest inspection covers and misses, who may do it (licensing varies by state) and when to book it, with state rules.

guides.title: Buying a home in Australia: the steps, state by state
guides.description: The steps to buy a home in Australia, and where they differ: contract, cooling-off, disclosure and settlement rules in NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT and NT.

guides.title: Buying at auction in Australia: the rules by state
guides.description: How an auction works in Australia: bidder registration, vendor bids, reserve, deposit and no cooling-off, with the rules of NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS and ACT.

guides.title: Capital gains tax and your main residence (CGT)
guides.description: When the main residence exemption removes CGT on selling your Australian home: the 6-year absence rule, partial exemption, 2 hectares, foreign residents.

guides.title: Contract of sale and exchange: what you sign, by state
guides.description: What a contract of sale contains, how exchange works, and what each state makes the seller hand over: section 32 in VIC, Form 1 in SA, and more.

guides.title: Conveyance duty in the ACT and the Home Buyer Concession
guides.description: ACT eligible home buyers pay no conveyance duty from 1 July 2026. Owner-occupier rates, the 5-year ownership test and the 1-year residence rule.

guides.title: Cooling-off period when buying a home, by state
guides.description: How long you can back out of a home purchase in Australia, what it costs and when it does not apply (auctions) in NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS and the ACT.

guides.title: Council rates in Australia: how they work, by state
guides.description: Council rates are set locally on a state valuation. How they work by state and territory, Victoria's 2.75% cap for 2026-27, the NSW rate peg and how to object.

guides.title: Home loan deposit and lenders mortgage insurance
guides.description: How the deposit, the loan-to-value ratio and lenders mortgage insurance (LMI) fit together in Australia, and the federal ways to buy with a smaller deposit.

guides.title: Property transfer duty in Tasmania: rates and relief
guides.description: Tasmanian property transfer duty: rates up to $4.50 per $100 above $725,000, the end of first home relief on 30 June 2026 and the new $20,000 grant.

guides.title: First home buyer stamp duty concessions in each state
guides.description: Compare first home buyer duty relief across the eight states and territories: thresholds, conditions and what changed in 2026 in WA, QLD, ACT and TAS.

guides.title: First home owner grants compared across the states
guides.description: The first home owner grant is a state payment, not a federal one. Amounts, price caps and dates in NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, TAS, NT and the ACT as at 14 October 2026.

guides.title: First Home Super Saver Scheme (FHSS): how it works
guides.description: Save for a first home through voluntary super: $15,000 a year, $50,000 in total. How the ATO release works, tax withheld, deadlines, eligibility.

guides.title: Foreign buyers and FIRB approval for a home
guides.description: Federal rules for foreign persons buying a home: who needs approval, the ban on established dwellings to 30 June 2029, 2026-27 fees and the vacancy fee.

guides.title: Foreign purchaser surcharge duty in each state
guides.description: Foreign buyers of homes pay an extra duty on top of stamp duty in most states: 9% in NSW, 8% in Victoria, Queensland and Tasmania, 7% in WA. State comparison.

guides.title: Foreign resident capital gains withholding (15%)
guides.description: When buying Australian property from a foreign resident, 15% of the price must be paid to the ATO at settlement. How clearance certificates and variations work.

guides.title: Australian Government 5% Deposit Scheme (Home Guarantee)
guides.description: Buy with a 5% deposit (2% for single parents) and no LMI under the federal scheme run by Housing Australia: eligibility, price caps by state and how to apply.

guides.title: Home loan pre-approval in Australia: what it is and isn't
guides.description: Pre-approval (conditional approval) shows what a lender may lend you. How long it lasts, why it is no guarantee, and how it fits with auctions and cooling-off.

guides.title: Home loan serviceability buffer: APRA's 3-point test
guides.description: Lenders must test your repayments at least 3 percentage points above the loan rate. How APRA's buffer, the debt-to-income limit and ASIC's rules work.

guides.title: Land tax by state: thresholds, home exemption, surcharges
guides.description: Land tax thresholds and rates in each state and territory, the main residence exemption and foreign or absentee surcharges. The NT has no land tax.

guides.title: Land titles register and title search in Australia
guides.description: What the land titles register shows, how to run a title search in each state, and the fees published in Queensland and Western Australia (2026-27).

guides.title: Land transfer duty in Victoria: rates and concessions
guides.description: Victoria's land transfer duty runs from 1.4% to 6.5%. Rates, the principal place of residence concession up to $550,000, first home buyers and off-the-plan.

guides.title: Rental bonds by state: caps, deadlines and who holds them
guides.description: Rental bond caps and lodgement deadlines in each state and territory: 4 weeks in most, one month in Victoria, and which authority holds the bond in each.

guides.title: Renting in NSW: bond, rent rises and notice periods
guides.description: NSW renting rules at 14 October 2026: bond up to 4 weeks' rent, one rent rise a year with 60 days' notice, a valid reason to end a lease, entry and pets.

guides.title: Renting in Queensland: bond, rent rises and notice
guides.description: Queensland renting rules at 14 October 2026: bond of 4 weeks' rent, one rent rise every 12 months with 2 months' notice, entry, housing standards and pets.

guides.title: Renting in SA, Tasmania, the ACT and the NT
guides.description: Renting rules in South Australia, Tasmania, the ACT and the Northern Territory compared: rent increases, notice to end a tenancy, entry, pets and tribunals.

guides.title: Renting in Victoria: bond, rent rises and notice
guides.description: Victorian renting rules at 14 October 2026: bond of one month's rent, 90 days' notice of a rent rise, a valid reason for a notice to vacate, entry and pets.

guides.title: Renting in Western Australia: bond, rent and notice
guides.description: Western Australian renting rules at 14 October 2026: bond of 4 weeks' rent, one rent rise a year with 60 days' notice, termination, entry and pets.

guides.title: Selling a home in Australia: what it costs, by state
guides.description: Agent commission is negotiable, not set by law, in the states checked. Selling cost items, a commission formula and the rules by state.

guides.title: Settlement and electronic conveyancing in Australia
guides.description: What happens at settlement when you buy a home, how long it takes, what is adjusted, and how electronic conveyancing works, by state.

guides.title: Stamp duty in the Northern Territory: formula and discount
guides.description: NT stamp duty is a formula up to $525,000, then 4.95%. The Territory home owner discount, the $50,000 new home grant and the 60-day lodgement deadline.

guides.title: Transfer duty in NSW: 2026/27 rates and first home buyers
guides.description: NSW transfer duty is a sliding scale from $1.25 to $5.50 per $100 above $1.29 million. 2026/27 rates, premium duty, payment deadline and first home buyers.

guides.title: Stamp duty in South Australia: how to find your figure
guides.description: South Australia's stamp duty is set by RevenueSA. Stamp duty relief for first home buyers of new homes, the $15,000 grant, and what to check before you sign.

guides.title: Strata title and body corporate: what to check by state
guides.description: Buying an apartment in Australia: owners corporation, body corporate or strata company, levies, by-laws and the certificates to ask for, by state.

guides.title: Transfer duty in Queensland: rates and home concessions
guides.description: Queensland transfer duty runs from nil to $5.75 per $100 over $1 million. Rates, home and first home concessions and the August 2026 citizenship rule.

guides.title: Transfer duty in Western Australia: rates and first home
guides.description: WA transfer duty runs from $1.90 per $100 to $5.15 per $100 above $725,000. Rates, the first home owner rate from 7 May 2026 and the 7% foreign surcharge.

guides.title: Vendor disclosure when selling a home, by state
guides.description: What a seller must give the buyer: Section 32 in Victoria, NSW contract documents, Queensland Form 2, SA Form 1, ACT documents, WA, NT and Tasmania.

professions.title: Building inspectors in Australia: pre-purchase rules
professions.description: Only Queensland licenses pre-purchase building inspectors among the states we could read. What NSW, SA and others say, how to check, and what to ask.

professions.title: Conveyancers in Australia: licences by state
professions.description: Who can do conveyancing in each state, where a licence is required (NSW, Victoria, WA, NT), which register to check, and what we could not confirm.

professions.title: Mortgage brokers in Australia: ASIC licence and register
professions.description: Mortgage brokers are regulated federally by ASIC. What the credit licence and best interests duty mean, how to check a broker, and what to ask.

professions.title: Property valuers in Australia: who is licensed where
professions.description: Valuer rules differ by state: registration in Queensland, a licence in WA, a qualification rule in Tasmania, none in NSW. Registers and questions to ask.

professions.title: Real estate agents in Australia: licences and registers
professions.description: Who licenses real estate agents in each state and territory, which register to check before you sign, and what each register's published terms say.
